questions.question: When driving in fog, rain, or snow, use:

options.text: Low beams.
High beams.
Fog lights only.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beams.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, and snow. High beams reflect back at you in bad weather, making it hard to see the road.

questions.question: By law, every vehicle (except motorcycles) must have:

options.text: Brakes that do not lock under any condition.
A foot brake and an emergency or parking brake.
A parking brake that can stop the vehicle within legal limits.

questions.correctAnswerText: A foot brake and an emergency or parking brake.
questions.explanation: All vehicles must have two brakes: a regular foot brake and a parking brake.

questions.question: You are in a left turn lane at an intersection with oncoming traffic. You should:

options.text: Move to the left of the center lane.
Signal before you reach the intersection.
Turn your front wheels left to prepare for the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal before you reach the intersection.
questions.explanation: Signal about 100 feet before turning. Keep your wheels straight until it is safe to turn. This way, if another car hits you from behind, you won't be pushed into oncoming traffic.

questions.question: For a second DUI conviction, the minimum jail time is:

options.text: Five days.
20 days.
45 days.

questions.correctAnswerText: 45 days.
questions.explanation: A second DUI conviction results in a jail sentence of at least 45 days, up to 11 months and 29 days.

questions.question: Alcohol is:

options.text: A stimulant.
An antihistamine.
A depressant.

questions.correctAnswerText: A depressant.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant. It slows your thinking and makes your reflexes slower and less reliable.

questions.question: When turning left at a corner, yield to:

options.text: Other vehicles also turning left.
All vehicles coming toward you.
Pedestrians on the sidewalk waiting to walk.

questions.correctAnswerText: All vehicles coming toward you.
questions.explanation: When turning left, you must yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and all other vehicles moving on their green light.

questions.question: If your tires lose contact with the road, you should:

options.text: Slow down by shifting to a lower gear.
Take your foot off the gas pedal.
Slow down by pumping the brakes hard and fast.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take your foot off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: If your tires lose grip, ease off the gas and do not use the brakes. Wait until your tires grip the road again before stopping or turning.

questions.question: Regulatory signs are what color:

options.text: Green.
Yellow.
White.

questions.correctAnswerText: White.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs tell drivers what laws they must follow. They are usually white squares or rectangles with black, red, or green text or symbols.

questions.question: If the light turns red while you are in the intersection waiting to turn left, you should:

options.text: Stop and wait for the light to turn green.
Back up out of the intersection if you can.
Turn left when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn left when it is safe.
questions.explanation: If you are already in the intersection when the light turns red, complete your left turn when it is safe. Yield to all oncoming traffic before turning.

questions.question: If your vehicle is hit from behind, you should not:

options.text: Release your seat belt.
Brace yourself.
Press your head against the head restraint.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release your seat belt.
questions.explanation: Keep your seat belt on. Press your head against the head restraint and brace yourself against the seat. Hold the steering wheel firmly and be ready to brake to avoid hitting another vehicle.

questions.question: When you leave an alley or driveway to enter traffic, what should you do?

options.text: Stop only if you see pedestrians on the sidewalk.
Stop before you drive onto the sidewalk.
Expect pedestrians to move out of your way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before you drive onto the sidewalk.
questions.explanation: You must stop before driving onto a sidewalk when leaving an alley, driveway, or parking lot. Pedestrians and other traffic have the right-of-way.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road ends ahead.
You must turn either right or left.
A four-way intersection is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must turn either right or left.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells drivers that the road splits ahead. You must choose to go either right or left.

questions.question: On an interstate, how can you avoid traffic coming from on-ramps on your right?

options.text: Move to the left lane.
Slow down.
Keep your speed and position the same.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the left lane.
questions.explanation: When you see an on-ramp ahead, move to the left lane when it is safe. This allows vehicles to merge onto the highway from the right.

questions.question: What is the penalty for a first DUI conviction?

options.text: A $100 fine, 24 hours in jail, and a six-month license suspension.
A $500 fine, 12 hours in jail, and a three-month license suspension.
A $350 fine, 48 hours in jail, and a one-year license suspension.

questions.correctAnswerText: A $350 fine, 48 hours in jail, and a one-year license suspension.
questions.explanation: A first DUI conviction results in at least 48 hours in jail (or seven days if your BAC was 0.20 or higher), a fine between $350 and $1,500, and a one-year license suspension.

questions.question: When traffic is moving at 50 to 55 mph, how can you avoid accidents?

options.text: Drive a few miles per hour faster than other vehicles.
Drive at the same speed as the traffic around you.
Drive a few miles per hour slower than other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive at the same speed as the traffic around you.
questions.explanation: Drive at the same speed as other traffic when that speed is within the speed limit. Vehicles moving at the same speed in the same direction cannot crash into each other. Crashes happen when vehicles drive at different speeds.

questions.question: In bad weather, what should you do?

options.text: Steer off the road.
Drive in a low gear.
Steer and brake slowly and smoothly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer and brake slowly and smoothly.
questions.explanation: In bad weather, do not slam on the brakes or make sharp turns. These actions make it harder to control your vehicle.

questions.question: In recent years, have fatal crashes caused by alcohol in Tennessee gone up or down?

options.text: Gone up.
Gone down.
Stayed the same.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gone down.
questions.explanation: In 2015, 34 percent of traffic deaths in Tennessee involved alcohol. By 2016, this number dropped to 27 percent.

questions.question: When can you legally turn left at a red light after stopping?

options.text: When you are on a two-way street and turning onto a two-way street.
When you are on a one-way street and turning onto another one-way street.
When you yield to all other traffic at the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are on a one-way street and turning onto another one-way street.
questions.explanation: After stopping, you may turn left at a red light only if you are on a one-way street and turning onto another one-way street. Make sure there are no signs that prohibit this turn.

questions.question: When driving at night on a poorly lit street, what should you do?

options.text: Drive slowly enough that you can stop within the light from your headlights.
Use high beams to see vehicles ahead better.
Keep your dashboard lights bright so other drivers can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slowly enough that you can stop within the light from your headlights.
questions.explanation: You cannot see as far at night as during the day. Drive slowly enough that you can stop your vehicle within the area lit by your headlights.

questions.question: You are behind a motorcycle and want to pass. What must you do?

options.text: Stay in the right lane because the motorcycle is small and doesn't use much space.
Honk your horn to make the motorcycle move to the shoulder.
Move completely into the left lane before and during the pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move completely into the left lane before and during the pass.
questions.explanation: Give a motorcycle a full lane when you pass. Do not try to share the lane. Moving back too soon can force the rider to swerve right into traffic or off the road.

questions.question: Your car's rear end starts skidding to the left. What should you do?

options.text: Steer to the right.
Steer to the left.
Tap your brakes lightly and shift into neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer to the left.
questions.explanation: If your car skids, take your foot off the brake and steer in the direction you want to go. If the rear skids left, steer left. This will straighten your car.

questions.question: You are entering a freeway. How should you check traffic on the freeway?

options.text: Using your rearview and side mirrors.
Using your rearview mirror.
Using your side mirror and looking over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using your side mirror and looking over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Use your side mirror and look over your shoulder to see traffic when entering a freeway.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Road construction or maintenance area.
Side road.
Railroad ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road construction or maintenance area.
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped orange signs warn of hazards in construction or maintenance areas.

questions.question: To turn quickly, where should your hands be on the steering wheel?

options.text: On opposite sides of the steering wheel.
Next to each other on the top of the steering wheel.
On the top and bottom of the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: On opposite sides of the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: Place both hands on opposite sides of the steering wheel. This position helps you turn safely on highways.

questions.question: When are streets and highways most slippery?

options.text: When it has been raining hard for several hours.
When they are clean and dry.
Just after it starts to rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just after it starts to rain.
questions.explanation: Roads are most slippery when rain first starts. The water mixes with oil and chemicals on the road that have not washed away yet. Drive carefully when it first rains.

questions.question: When you see a flashing yellow light at an intersection, what should you do?

options.text: Yield to all traffic before crossing the intersection.
Stop, then enter the intersection when it is safe.
Slow down and cross the intersection carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and cross the intersection carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.question: When should you check your rearview mirrors?

options.text: Often to see how traffic is moving behind you.
To see if a vehicle is in your blind spot.
Only when you are slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often to see how traffic is moving behind you.
questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirrors often so you know where vehicles are near you.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Intersection.
Road curve.
Right turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Intersection.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs with black markings alert you to immediate hazards. This sign warns that another road crosses the highway ahead.

questions.question: You face a green traffic light, but traffic blocks the intersection ahead. What should you do?

options.text: Turn left and find another route.
Stay out of the intersection until traffic clears.
Follow the other vehicles and enter the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay out of the intersection until traffic clears.
questions.explanation: Do not enter the intersection if traffic blocks it, even if the light is green. If you are trapped in the intersection when the light changes to red, you block other traffic and can get a ticket.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you never do?

options.text: Cross the centerline in an intersection.
Check your blind spots by looking over your left or right shoulder.
Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cross the centerline in an intersection.
questions.explanation: Never change lanes in an intersection. Before changing lanes, check your blind spot and look for drivers trying to enter the same lane.
